en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
context: Asking a stranger politely on a train.
explain: 'Is this seat taken' is the usual polite phrase to ask if someone is sitting there.

en: We have already checked in online.
explain: 'Have checked in' shows the action is done. 'Already' means earlier than expected.

en: The ticket collector is coming to check tickets.
context: Warning your friend on a train.
explain: 'Is coming' shows something is about to happen. 'To check' tells the purpose.

en: Where is the nearest petrol bunk?
tamil: பக்கத்தில் இருக்கிற பெட்ரோல் பங்க் எங்க இருக்கு?
context: Asking while driving a bike or car.
explain: 'Nearest' means the closest one. 'Where is' asks about a place.

en: Our bus broke down on the highway.
explain: 'Broke down' is the past of 'break down'. It means stopped working.

en: You should book train tickets early.
tamil: நீங்க ட்ரெயின் டிக்கெட்டை சீக்கிரம் புக் பண்ணணும்.
explain: 'Should' is used for advice. 'Early' tells when it is best to do it.

en: I have never travelled by flight.
explain: 'Have never' talks about your whole life up to now. It means not even once.

en: Could you stop here, please?
explain: 'Could you' is polite. Adding 'please' at the end makes it softer.

en: What is the check-out time?
explain: This question asks for a fixed time. Hotels use 'check-out' for the time you leave.

en: The auto driver asked for double the fare.
tamil: ஆட்டோ டிரைவர் ரெண்டு மடங்கு கட்டணம் கேட்டார்.
explain: 'Double the fare' means two times the normal price. 'Asked for' means requested.

en: I'll call you when I reach the station.
tamil: ஸ்டேஷன் போய் சேர்ந்ததும் உனக்கு கால் பண்றேன்.
explain: 'I'll' is short for 'I will'. After 'when' we use a present form: 'reach'.

en: Is the flight on time?
context: Checking at the airport or on the phone.
explain: 'On time' means not late. This is a short, common travel question.

en: Don't forget to carry your ID card.
tamil: உங்க ஐடி கார்டு எடுத்துட்டு போக மறந்துடாதீங்க.
context: Reminding a friend before a journey.
explain: 'Don't forget to' is a friendly reminder. It is followed by a simple verb.

en: There is no direct bus to that village.
context: Explaining the route to a visitor.
explain: 'There is no' says something does not exist. 'Direct' means without changing.

en: We are going to visit Ooty next month.
tamil: அடுத்த மாசம் நாங்க ஊட்டி போகப் போறோம்.
explain: 'Are going to' is for plans you have already made. 'Next month' shows the time.

en: The hotel staff were very helpful.
explain: 'Staff' is a group, so here we use 'were'. 'Helpful' means ready to help.

en: Can you share the location on WhatsApp?
context: Asking a driver or friend how to find a place.
explain: 'Can you' asks for help. 'Share the location' is very common in India.

en: My train gets in at midnight.
explain: We use present simple for timetables. 'Gets in' means arrives at the station.

en: Please take the second right after the temple.
explain: Use ordinal numbers like 'second' to count turnings. 'After the temple' is a landmark.

en: They are checking everyone's bags at the airport.
explain: 'Are checking' shows it is happening now. 'Everyone's' shows the bags belong to everyone.

en: Is breakfast included in the room rent?
context: Asking before you book a hotel.
explain: 'Included' means already part of the price. This is useful before you pay.
